conviction_note: Six of seven prior reactions were positive but the single negative was -13.78% off a beat-and-raise three months ago, and the corpus identifies exactly why: the back-half guide is built on tariff rates reverting to start-of-year levels. The stock has since recovered to within 7.5% of its high and above most sell-side targets with that assumption never revisited in any captured coverage, so a bit over half the 5.59% median, negative.

findings.finding: Five Below's back-half guidance rests on an explicit management assumption that tariffs revert - CFO Daniel Sullivan on the 2026-06-03 call: 'We have assumed for the back half of the year tariff rates that return to levels that they were at, at the start of our fiscal year' - which is what made the stock fall 13.78% on a quarter with revenue +32%, comps +22.7% and a raised guide; the stock has since rallied to 7.48% off its 52-week high on three sell-side upgrades and no captured item has revisited the tariff assumption since 2026-06-04, and this print is the first one that sets guidance for the very half that assumption covers.
findings.corpus_ref: docs/e5819b95e3d776b71640851bff5228f85b1ca239.txt (StockTwits sweep 20260830T083745Z), the CFO quote at the message of 2026-06-04T10:14:51Z and the analyst framing at 2026-06-04T04:41:37Z; upgrade sequence at 2026-07-09 (Mizuho, Outperform, tgt $220), 2026-07-21 (Bernstein, Outperform, tgt $250), 2026-08-13 (Jefferies, Buy, tgt $350) and the lone downgrade at 2026-08-25 (Loop Capital, Hold, tgt $250)
findings.why_not_priced: The quote is three months old and was priced once, in the -13.78% June reaction - and then unpriced again by a 75.5% rally off the low that took the stock to $243.08, above the Mizuho ($220), Bernstein ($250 on a spot of 243) and Loop ($250) targets and leaving only the Jefferies $350 above it. The upgrade notes in the corpus argue merchandising, viral demand and a sub-20x multiple; none of them addresses whether the tariff reversion assumption held. That is the mechanism: the market has re-rated the stock on the strength of the business while the guidance bridge to H2 still depends on a policy assumption nobody has re-underwritten, and the print is where that bridge either holds or is cut. If it were priced, the stock would not be a few percent from its high at the multiple the corpus's own bears keep pointing at, and the five-day run-in would not be the only sign of hesitation.
findings.independence: Two other corpus items point the same way from different sources: Mizuho's own note forecasts H2 comps of 8-9% and adjusted EPS of $9.22 'above consensus', i.e. the bull case explicitly needs H2 to beat, and Wolfe Research separately cut FIVE to hold in June (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/23/the-clubs-top-10-things-to-watch-in-the-stock-market-tuesday.html). A weaker, direction-unknown pointer: eight Form 4s were filed on 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-05 with the stock near its high, and no bodies are stored so I cannot say whether they were sales.
